device.name: Rachio Controller
device.notes: The observed Rachio controller advertises HomeKit HAP over mDNS with a model string matching Rachio-B68A9A. The HAP accessory ID is stable across IP changes and should be used for identity. Port 80 is open on the device, but this spec currently documents local discovery rather than a complete unauthenticated control protocol. Silicon lineage: Gen 1 = Electric Imp platform (BlinkUp optical provisioning; cloud end-of-life 2024), Gen 2 = AzureWave CU288 / Marvell (FCC ID TLZ-CU288), Gen 3 = Rachio's own FCC ID 2AOTB-ZULWC, dual-band Wi-Fi plus a 900 MHz radio for the Wireless Flow Meter. Native HomeKit exists only on Rachio 3. In-the-wild firmware build: iro3-firmware-hk-5-632 ("hk" = HomeKit). Rachio's 2025 Smart Lighting Controller uses Matter/Thread — the vendor is migrating new products away from HomeKit.

methods.description: Gen 2 flow (decompiled com.rachio.iro v2.8; constants re-confirmed in the current decompiled app, com.rachio.prov.gen2): the phone joins the unit's setup AP (SSID prefix "Rachio"; device AP at 192.168.10.1), then GET /rachio/iroinfo (device info incl. salt), POST /prov/secure-session (Curve25519 ECDH; session key derived from the shared secret + device salt + serial number — the serial acts as PIN), GET /prov/net-info?session_id=N (scan results, AES-CTR encrypted), POST /prov/network?session_id=N (home SSID/passphrase, AES-CTR encrypted) and POST /sys/time (epoch sync). Bodies are form-urlencoded; crypto is AES/CTR/NoPadding with Curve25519 ECDH, as re-confirmed in the current app.

credential_encryption.key_derivation: Curve25519 ECDH shared secret + device salt + device serial number (serial acts as PIN); session-scoped key.
credential_encryption.notes: Setup SSID is 'Rachio-' plus the last 3 MAC bytes (6 hex chars, uppercase), derived from the MAC in the current decompiled app.

steps.action: Join the controller's setup AP (SSID "Rachio-XXXXXX", XXXXXX = last 3 MAC bytes uppercase); the device is at 192.168.10.1.
GET /rachio/iroinfo for device info and salt.
POST /prov/secure-session to establish the Curve25519 ECDH session (serial number as PIN).
POST /prov/network?session_id=N with the home Wi-Fi credentials (AES-CTR encrypted).

steps.notes: Gen 2 verified from the decompiled app (v2.8 flow, constants re-confirmed in the current app); not replayed on hardware.

methods.description: Gen 3 flow (decompiled current app, com.rachio.prov.gen3): the phone joins the unit's setup Wi-Fi, then talks HTTPS JSON to the device — POST https://<deviceMac>/<endpoint> with a custom DNS resolver, a pinned root CA shipped in the app assets (rachioBroker_rootCA.pem) and auth header "x-api-key: <serial uppercase>". Endpoints: info, config, conn, schedule, time, done, remove, fwupdate. The config body carries the home ssid/pass in cleartext JSON (protected only by the pinned TLS session); time carries the epoch. The conn poll exposes the device's connection state machine — WIFI_CONNECTED → DNS_SUCCESS → TLS_CONNECTED → MQTT_CONNECTED → MQTT_SUBSCRIBED → FULLY_CONNECTED — confirming the Gen 3 cloud path is MQTT. App-side provisioning states run CONNECT → SETTINGTIME → CONFIGURING → WAITINGFORWIFI → CHECKING → COMPLETE, with a final POST done.

credential_encryption.algorithm: TLS with a pinned vendor root CA
credential_encryption.notes: Wi-Fi credentials travel as cleartext JSON fields (ssid, pass) inside the pinned-TLS POST body; no application-layer encryption like Gen 2.

steps.action: Join the controller's setup Wi-Fi (SSID "Rachio-XXXXXX", XXXXXX = last 3 MAC bytes uppercase).
POST https://<deviceMac>/time with the current epoch (JSON, pinned CA, x-api-key header).
POST https://<deviceMac>/config with the home Wi-Fi ssid and pass as JSON.
Poll https://<deviceMac>/conn until the device reports Wi-Fi then MQTT connected (state machine ending at FULLY_CONNECTED).

steps.notes: Derived from the decompiled app; not replayed on hardware. The pinned CA means third-party clients must extract or replace it to talk to the device.

methods.description: HomeKit pairing using the 8-digit setup code generated and displayed in the Rachio app (Controller Settings → HomeKit; reportedly iOS-only), which provides cloud-free local control once paired.

steps.action: Perform a HAP pair-setup against the advertised _hap._tcp service using the app-displayed setup code.
steps.notes: Not implemented in this project; the most promising route to local control.

setup.notes: Gen 2 onboarding is documented from the decompiled vendor app (com.rachio.iro v2.8, UCLA ECE209AS): SoftAP provisioning with a Curve25519 secure session (see below). The Gen 3 flow is now also documented from the decompiled current app (com.rachio.prov.gen3): HTTPS JSON POSTs to the setup AP under a pinned CA, no Curve25519 session (see below). Neither flow has been replayed against hardware. What is confirmed from the LAN probe is the post-setup state: the controller advertises a HomeKit HAP service, and HAP pairing gives cloud-free local control. The HomeKit setup code is NOT printed on the device — it is generated and displayed in the Rachio app (Controller Settings → HomeKit; reportedly iOS-only), so HAP pairing depends on the vendor app at least once.

rejoin.notes: Unverified. The onboarding flows are now documented from the decompiled app, but whether a configured unit accepts in-place re-provisioning without a reset is still unknown — assume reset-and-reprovision.

testing.notes: Probed live 2026-08-14 against the real controller (Rachio-B68A9A): _hap._tcp mDNS re-observed with the documented TXT identity keys (id=0A:01:0A:36:39:1E, md=Rachio-B68A9A, pv=1.1, sf=1 — i.e. currently UNPAIRED/discoverable). The port-80 service is HAP and nothing else: GET /, /accessories and /pair-setup all answer HTTP 470 (HAP connection-authorization-required), confirming there is no unauthenticated local control surface. No pairing was attempted — the HomeKit setup code only exists in the vendor app, and pairing an unpaired unit out from under its owner would be hostile. SoftAP provisioning flows remain unexercised.

http_endpoints.description: TCP port 80 was observed open. Control path is not yet documented as a complete local unauthenticated REST API.
